AIM.1.reason: Each window sample is taken at PWM falling edges, so the cp_delay value BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-off is counted. When cp_sync is high only during the low-side period (or only during the high-side period), fault_count_*_out and window_trip/window_trip_SS differ from the valley-sampled reference.

AIM.2.description: The blanking history cp_delay advances once per switching cycle (on pwm_rise) instead of once per clock, so the lookback is BLANK_CLKS cycles rather than BLANK_CLKS clocks.
AIM.2.reason: While active, the sample added at each pwm_rise is the comparator state from several switching cycles earlier, not from a few clocks before turn-on. AIM.4.reason: In S_SS, when cp_sync at pwm_rise differs from cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1], the count gains or loses one against the window. fault_count_ss_out drifts, and can wrap when the bit leaves 32 cycles later, so window_trip_SS asserts or fails to assert wrongly.

AIM.7.description: The soft-start window and count are cleared on every S_RUN sample, instead of being held through S_RUN for telemetry.
AIM.7.reason: After the S_SS -> S_RUN transition, fault_count_ss_out drops to 0 at the first pwm_rise in S_RUN. It should keep the value reached at the end of soft start.

AIM.8.description: The S_RUN window is also advanced during S_SS, so it enters S_RUN pre-loaded with soft-start overcurrent history.

AIM.9.description: The idle clear of both windows is qualified by pwm_rise like the update branches, so the windows clear only if PWM is still toggling while neither state is active.

AIM.10.description: The idle clear resets the two counts but leaves the two shift registers holding the faulted history from before the hiccup.
AIM.10.reason: After a retry, the old 1s shift out of the window and are subtracted from a count that was cleared to 0. fault_count_*_out wrap to a large value and window_trip / window_trip_SS assert without any new overcurrent.

AIM.11.description: window_trip is gated by 'not in soft start' instead of 'in S_RUN', so it is not suppressed in the idle states.

AIM.12.description: window_trip_SS is gated by 'converter switching' (S_SS or S_RUN) instead of S_SS only, so the frozen soft-start count can trip it during S_RUN.
AIM.12.reason: If fault_count_ss reached trip_ss on the edge the FSM left S_SS, or trip_ss is lowered during S_RUN below the held count, window_trip_SS is high throughout S_RUN.
